topic: How can satellite link budgets be optimized for high throughput and low latency in global aeronautical coverage?
consensus_response: To optimize satellite link budgets, it is essential to balance bandwidth against fixed latency. QoS-OSPF with RSVP manages available capacity but does not consider high fixed latencies. Bandwidth Delay Satellite Routing is ideal for LEO networks, considering both delay and bandwidth. Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) and Satellite Adaptive Coding and Modulation (ACM) adapt to real-time channel conditions, reducing congestion and latency. Network Slicing allocates dedicated resources for critical applications. By combining these techniques with an enhanced path selection mechanism aware of satellite link characteristics, optimal paths can be chosen for all traffic flows or aggregates, optimizing performance in global aeronautical coverage.
reference_context: Satellite links have varying link conditions, including high fixed latency, which negatively impacts QoS. Existing techniques focus on managing available capacity but do not consider latency. Bandwidth Delay Satellite Routing is suitable for LEO networks, considering both delay and bandwidth.
